findings.issue_text: **`app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`** (script block): `request.referer` is interpolated unescaped into a JS string literal: `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. `ensure_embeddable` only checks that `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` — it never validates or escapes the rest of the URL (path/query/fragment). Since `Referer` is attacker-settable (e.g., via a page hosted on the trusted host that reflects a query string, an open redirect on that domain, or simply a crafted request bypassing browser referer semantics), a value like `http://embeddable-host/'};</script><script>alert(document.cookie)</script>` breaks out of both the string literal and the `<script>` tag, yielding reflected XSS inside the iframe (and, via `postMessage`, potential influence over the parent page). Fix: JSON/JS-escape the value, e.g. `<%= raw request.referer.to_s.to_json %>`, and/or restrict to the validated origin string derived from `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` rather than echoing the raw referer.

**`app/models/topic_embed.rb#absolutize_urls`**: only rewrites `href`/`src` that start with `/`; it does not strip or validate dangerous schemes (`javascript:`, `data:`) on `a[href]`/`img[src]`. `import_remote` passes `attributes: %w[href src]` to Readability, which whitelists the attribute *names* but not their *values*, so a crafted source page/feed item containing `<a href="javascript:alert(1)">` will be imported and rendered verbatim (`cook_method: raw_html` skips the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline entirely — `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged). This is stored XSS served to every viewer of the embedded topic. Fix: sanitize/whitelist URL schemes (`http`/`https` only) when absolutizing, or route imported HTML through the standard sanitizer even in `raw_html` mode.

**`lib/tasks/disqus.thor`**: the `--category`/`-c` option and the `category_id` lookup were deleted, and topic creation was switched from `PostCreator.new(... category: category_id)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which has no category support at all. This silently removes existing functionality for anyone using this import task with categorized imports; it's also outside the stated scope ("embed URL handling and validation"). If intentional, it should be called out explicitly (and ideally `TopicEmbed.import`/`import_remote` should accept an optional category) rather than being a side effect of the refactor.

**`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb#ensure_embeddable`**: host comparison (`URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) is case-sensitive; hostnames are case-insensitive, so `EXAMPLE.com` referer would be wrongly rejected against `example.com`. Same applies to `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`. Normalize with `.downcase` on both sides.

**`app/models/topic_embed.rb#import`**: `contents << "\n<hr>\n..."` mutates the caller-supplied string in place. Callers (`PollFeed#poll_feed`, `import_remote`) happen to pass fresh strings today, but this is a latent footgun if a caller reuses/caches a content string across calls. Prefer `contents = contents + "..."` or `+=`.

**`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb#poll_feed` / `TopicEmbed#import_remote`**: `open(url)` (open-uri) has no timeout configured. A slow/unresponsive feed or remote host can hang the hourly `PollFeed` job (and the inline `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` call made synchronously from `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`) with no bound, tying up a Sidekiq worker. Consider `open(url, read_timeout: ..., open_timeout: ...)`.

**`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb#best`**: no rescue around `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)`; if the `TopicEmbed` row references a topic that was since deleted, this will 500 instead of degrading gracefully (e.g., falling back to "loading"/re-retrieve).

Unrelated changes bundled into this PR: `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` gained `force: true` (risky in general to retroactively edit an already-applied migration — drops-and-recreates the table if re-run), and `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` had only whitespace/EOF-newline churn. Neither belongs to "embed URL handling"; worth splitting out or at least calling out in the PR description.

**Testing gaps**: no test covers `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` edge cases (scheme filtering, port handling), `import_remote`, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http`, or the actual item-parsing logic inside `PollFeed#poll_feed` (only the top-level gating conditions are tested via mocks). The XSS/referer-escaping issue above has no regression test either.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/models/topic_embed.rb#absolutize_urls`**: only rewrites `href`/`src` that start with `/`; it does not strip or validate dangerous schemes (`javascript:`, `data:`) on `a[href]`/`img[src]`. `import_remote` passes `attributes: %w[href src]` to Readability, which whitelists the attribute *names* but not their *values*, so a crafted source page/feed item containing `<a href="javascript:alert(1)">` will be imported and rendered verbatim (`cook_method: raw_html` skips the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline entirely — `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged). Fix: sanitize/whitelist URL schemes (`http`/`https` only) when absolutizing, or route imported HTML through the standard sanitizer even in `raw_html` mode.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook path where `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `TopicEmbed.import` sets `cook_method: :raw_html` and stores `raw` as `absolutize_urls(url, contents)`, but `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative URLs starting with `/` and performs no scheme/value sanitization for `a[href]` or `img[src]`. `import_remote` (Readability) and `PollFeed` both ingest external HTML content; Readability’s `attributes: %w[href src]` only whitelists attribute names, not safe URL schemes. The embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so attacker-controlled `href="javascript:..."` / `src="data:..."` can be stored and served verbatim, enabling stored XSS. This is directly verifiable from the diff’s new raw_html bypass and lack of sanitization in `absolutize_urls`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`lib/tasks/disqus.thor`**: the `--category`/`-c` option and the `category_id` lookup were deleted, and topic creation was switched from `PostCreator.new(... category: category_id)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which has no category support at all. If intentional, it should be called out explicitly (and ideally `TopicEmbed.import`/`import_remote` should accept an optional category) rather than being a side effect of the refactor.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` explicitly removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'`, deletes the `category_id` lookup based on that option, and replaces `PostCreator.new(..., category: category_id)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. In this diff, `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicEmbed.import` do not accept or pass through any category information, so the import task can no longer place imported topics into a user-specified category. That is a concrete behavior regression for anyone using `--category/-c`, and it is not otherwise compensated for in the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb#ensure_embeddable`**: host comparison (`URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) is case-sensitive; hostnames are case-insensitive, so `EXAMPLE.com` referer would be wrongly rejected against `example.com`. Same applies to `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`. Normalize with `.downcase` on both sides.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the referer host is compared via strict string inequality: `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Hostnames are case-insensitive, but Ruby string comparison is case-sensitive, and the code does not normalize either side. The same strict comparison exists in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` (`SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`). This can wrongly reject otherwise valid requests/URLs if the host casing differs (e.g., `EXAMPLE.com` vs `example.com`). Normalizing both sides (e.g., `.to_s.downcase`) would avoid the defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/models/topic_embed.rb#import`**: `contents << "\n<hr>\n..."` mutates the caller-supplied string in place. Callers (`PollFeed#poll_feed`, `import_remote`) happen to pass fresh strings today, but this is a latent footgun if a caller reuses/caches a content string across calls. Prefer `contents = contents + "..."` or `+=`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `TopicEmbed.import` doing `contents << "\n<hr>..."`, which mutates the passed-in String. However, in the added/modified call sites in this diff (`PollFeed#poll_feed` building `content = ...` and `import_remote` passing `doc.content`), there is no demonstrated reuse of the same String across calls, and the method does not store/reuse `contents` elsewhere. So while the mutation is a plausible “footgun” in general Ruby API design, it is speculative and not a verifiable bug/correctness defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb#poll_feed` / `TopicEmbed#import_remote`**: `open(url)` (open-uri) has no timeout configured. A slow/unresponsive feed or remote host can hang the hourly `PollFeed` job (and the inline `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` call made synchronously from `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`) with no bound, tying up a Sidekiq worker. Consider `open(url, read_timeout: ..., open_timeout: ...)`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple network fetches via `open-uri` without any timeout options: `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read`. These are executed in Sidekiq jobs (and `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` even calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously before doing another fetch), so a slow/unresponsive remote host can block a worker for an unbounded/undesirably long time. The lack of explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` is directly verifiable in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb#best`**: no rescue around `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)`; if the `TopicEmbed` row references a topic that was since deleted, this will 500 instead of degrading gracefully (e.g., falling back to "loading"/re-retrieve).

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the presence of a `topic_id` from `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is treated as sufficient to build `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)`. However, `topic_id_for_embed` only plucks the stored `topic_id` from `topic_embeds` and does not verify the topic still exists. Since the new migration adds `topic_embeds` without foreign key constraints and no `dependent: :destroy` cleanup is shown, a stale `topic_embeds.topic_id` can remain after a topic is deleted. In that case, `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` is very likely to raise (e.g., via `Topic.find(topic_id)`), producing a 500 with no rescue/fallback to re-retrieve or render `loading`.

Neither belongs to "embed URL handling"; worth splitting out or at least calling out in the PR description.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include unrelated migration churn: (1) `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` changes `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`, which will drop-and-recreate the table if that migration is ever re-run (e.g., `db:setup`, `db:reset`, recreating from schema), and it’s a retroactive edit to an existing migration unrelated to embed functionality. (2) `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` shows only whitespace/newline-only changes (and now lacks an EOF newline), which is also unrelated churn. This is verifiable directly from the diff and is a legitimate review concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Testing gaps**: no test covers `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` edge cases (scheme filtering, port handling), `import_remote`, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http`, or the actual item-parsing logic inside `PollFeed#poll_feed` (only the top-level gating conditions are tested via mocks). The XSS/referer-escaping issue above has no regression test either.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff adds non-trivial logic in several new/changed methods but the accompanying specs only cover a subset:
- `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` is only exercised indirectly via `TopicEmbed.import` with a single basic case; there are no direct tests for edge cases like non-default ports (code explicitly appends `:port`), different schemes, or other URL forms.
- `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (new) has no spec coverage.
- `TopicRetriever` specs cover `#retrieve` host/throttle gating by stubbing `retrieved_recently?`, but do not cover the actual work path in `perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http` (RSS polling branch and HTTP import).
- `Jobs::PollFeed` spec only tests `execute` gating conditions and never tests `poll_feed` parsing logic (`SimpleRSS.parse`, item iteration, link/id fallback, HTML unescaping/scrub, and `TopicEmbed.import` calls).
Thus, the stated “testing gaps” are directly verifiable from the diff (missing/insufficient tests for these behaviors).
